In this version, “ọ̀rọ̀ èyíkéyìí” (language as a tool of communication) is affirmed as the core function — not merely a medium, but the *purpose*. All other uses — poetic expression, ritual incantation, historical preservation, social bonding — are valuable, but they arise from and are subordinate to the fundamental act of sharing meaning.

The phrase is rendered in classical Yoruba orthography and rhythm, with the classical tonal markers preserved. The addition of “ṣoṣo” (vast, expansive) emphasizes that communication, in its fullest sense, encompasses not just information but emotion, intention, and worldview.

This is not just a proverb — it is a philosophy of language, rooted in African epistemology.
